explanation: For each true cell, the largest square ending there has side one plus the minimum side ending above, left and diagonally above-left. Track the greatest side and return its area.
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: A true cell can end a square of side s exactly when its top, left and diagonal predecessor squares all support side at least s−1. Taking one plus their minimum gives the largest feasible square at that cell; a false cell supports none. Every square has a lower-right corner, so the largest computed side gives the answer.
walkthrough: For [[true,true,false],[true,true,true],[false,true,true]], a 2×2 all-true square appears at the upper left and another at the lower right. No 3×3 square exists because two corner cells are false. Return area 4.
edgeCases: False cells reset the local square side to zero.
The returned quantity is area, not side length.
